name: noninterference_scroll_does_not_move_focus
description: NON-INTERFERENCE across the scroll/focus/selection seam: scrolling a container must move the scroll manager and re-arm the scrollbar fade in gpu_state, AND NOTHING ELSE. Focus stays where it was, no selection appears, no undo entry is recorded, no permission is subscribed. Every one of those is a coupling that would be invisible in the DOM, in the pixels and in the resource counters — a scroll that quietly cleared focus renders identically to one that did not. The baseline is taken 2000 ms after the mount so the mount's own scrollbar fade has already expired; the assertion then runs INSIDE the 500 ms fade delay that the scroll re-arms, which is what makes 'gpu_state moved' a deterministic statement rather than a race. Two-sided on purpose: if scroll or gpu_state stops moving here, this scenario has stopped exercising what it names and says so, instead of passing on a shrinking set.
